newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oks listing of President's store.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oks listing of President's store.

text.p: Taiwan's securities watchdog has approved the listing of the money-making chain store of President Enterprise following a half-year delay, officials said on Thursday.
"The Secuities and Exchange Commission gave its green light on Wednesday for the public stock offering for President Chain Store," a commission official contacted by Reuters said on telephone.
He said the chain store can register with relevant authorities for the marketing of its stocks.
President group leader Kao Chin-yen was not immediately available for comment as financial markets were all closed on the Labour Day on Thursday.
A broker reached by Reuters said the stock offering would enable President Enterprise to net at least T$3.5 billion in stock sales in 1997.
The chain store is expected to release 43.2 million shares, 50 percent would be offered through underwriters, while the rest through auctions, the broker said.
He said the underwriting price of the chain store share would cost at least T$90.

President Chain Store, which runs the 7-Eleven franchise in Taiwan, had been scheduled for listing at the end of 1996, but because of insider trading allegations, the company delayed its shre listing.
The chain store, the largest of all similar operations in Taiwan, has estimated its 1997 sales at T$33 billion, with a net profit of T$1l.4 billion.
The chain store's 1996 sales totaled T$29 billion with pre-tax profit at T$1.4 billion.
